newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends mixed after whippy day's trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends mixed after whippy day's trade.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.50 PCT (PREV 9.40) US 30-YR 6.43 (PREV 6.47)
* NZ bills sold at close, bonds flat to slightly stronger
* 11/06 bond puts in late rally
* Fall in qtrly retail sales fails to inspire short end
New Zealand debt markets ended the week mixed on Friday, with continued weakness in the money market and a late rally from the long bonds.
The 90-day bank bill rates and their corresponding futures contract parted company, with the former finishing five basis points higher at 9.10 percent and the latter climbing one point to 91.35.
The overnight cash rate rose to 9.50 percent from 9.40 percent.
Dealers said the session had been whippy, and the price action had been slightly disappointing given the market's promising start.
Weak retail trade data failed to boost languishing market sentiment.

Real, seasonally-adjusted retail sales fell 0.3 percent in the September quarter, against economists' forecasts of a 0.4 percent fall. Economists said the figures confirmed the general picture of a weakening in the economy and would be welcomed by the Reserve Bank.
"The market was bought on the open, got a bit long, couldn't rally on the good number, got sold off and now it's just come back a bit bid here," was how one money market dealer summarised the day.
Volumes were reasonably heavy.
Labour Party finance spokesperson Michael Cullen reiterated his call for a lower New Zealand dollar, saying the weak retail trade data added strength to the argument.
The kiwi dollar slipped to US$0.7098/05 from its 0.7120/27 open, and to 67.31 from 67.54 on its Trade Weighted Index.

One dealer said the comments had little effect on bills, with the impact of Cullen's view diluted each time he voiced it. Cullen made a strongly-worded statement on Thursday saying the overvalued dollar had to come down.

Meanwhile, the 11/06 bond put in a late run after a choppy performance. It ended at 7.15 percent, coming down sharply just before the close from a yield of 7.20 percent, and against a 7.12 percent low earlier in the session.
Dealers said New Zealand debt had put in a weaker than expected effort and continued to underperform other dollar bloc markets.
